articles.headline: Is Bijan Robinson the NFL's top RB? He is when he's in primetime
articles.description: Bijan Robinson has the most scrimmage yards per game in primetime, and he'll get a chance to keep it rolling on 'Monday Night Football' this week.
articles.headlineJa: ビジャン・ロビンソンはNFL最高のRBか？プライムタイムならその答えは「イエス」だ
articles.descriptionJa: ビジャン・ロビンソンはプライムタイムでの1試合平均スクリメージヤードでリーグトップを誇っており、今週の「マンデーナイトフットボール」でもその勢いを維持するチャンスを迎える。
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski shows high school football highlights of his players to the team on Fridays. For most, the glory days of high school set a bar few could match against NFL competition.

Then there's Bijan Robinson.

To be clear, Robinson was a superstar at Salpointe Catholic High School in Tucson, Arizona. He was the Gatorade Player of the Year as a senior in 2019. But Robinson's highlights on Friday nights don't match what he has done under the lights in the NFL.

Since the 1970 NFL/AFC merger, no player has more scrimmage yards per game in primetime than Robinson (145.4 in 11 games) with a minimum of five games, per ESPN Research. Barry Sanders is second with 126.3 scrimmage yards per game in 20 contests. OJ Simpson (123 in six games) and Jonathan Taylor (121.8 in 12 games) are third and fourth, respectively.

Robinson will try to keep it rolling Monday when the Falcons (1-2) travel to New Orleans (1-2) to face the Saints (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN).

"For me, whether it's primetime, whether it's a 1 o'clock game, they're all the same in terms of my mentality," Robinson said. "Everybody watches you on TV, and they watch you in the stands.

"I love what Kobe [Bryant] said: 'They paid to watch you, so you got to do your job on the field.'"

Robinson was remarkable against the Green Bay Packers on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 3, leading Atlanta to a 35-14 road win. He had 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns, and added another 19 yards on two receptions.

"He's an elite player," Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said. "He's one of the best in the league at any position." The Falcons signed Robinson to an offseason extension that briefly made him the highest-paid running back in NFL history. Robinson, the No. 8 pick in the 2023 draft, is under contract for three years with a base salary of $66.75 million ($22.3 million per season), which could go up to $75 million. The Detroit Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs has the highest average per year at $22.5 million.

"Bro, I don't know what to say," Packers running back Kaleb Johnson said after the Week 3 game. "He deserves every penny of that."

Robinson has picked up where he left off in 2025, when he was named first-team All-Pro. He once again leads the league in yards from scrimmage (467) and is second in rushing yards (349).

Last season, he had the two longest runs of his career -- 93 yards against the Los Angeles Rams and 81 yards against the Buffalo Bills -- on "Monday Night Football." Against the Minnesota Vikings on "Sunday Night Football" in 2025, Robinson had 168 scrimmage yards. Since Robinson debuted in 2023, he has over 20 scrimmage yards per game more than any other running back in primetime. More than Derrick Henry (123.9). More than Saquon Barkley (119.5).

articles.headline: Kylian Mbappé goes cycling despite José Mourinho warning
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has shared a video of himself riding a bicycle on social media, just days after his Real Madrid manager, José Mourinho, said players couldn't go cycling because of the injury risks involved.
articles.headlineJa: キリアン・エムバペ、ジョゼ・モウリーニョの警告を無視してサイクリングへ
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードのジョゼ・モウリーニョ監督が負傷リスクを理由に選手にサイクリングを禁じたわずか数日後、キリアン・エムバペが自身が自転車に乗る動画をSNSに投稿した。
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has shared a video of himself riding a bicycle on social media, just days after his Real Madrid manager, José Mourinho, said players couldn't go cycling because of the injury risks involved.

In an Instagram story posted on Sunday, Mbappé -- who is currently out of action after picking up an injury with France earlier in this international break -- filmed himself cycling, smiling and wearing a helmet, on what appeared to be a country road.

The video clip, which lasted just a few seconds and was accompanied by a 1970s song "The Good Guys, The Bad Guys" by the singer Michel Fugain, has been interpreted in the French media as a response to his critics.

Last month, Mourinho used bike riding as an example of the activities footballers must avoid, given their profession.

"You are a football player 24 hours a day," Mourinho told the Bet It Drives show. "Everything reflects the job. What you eat, what you drink, how you sleep, even things in your private life. You cannot ski. You cannot ride a bike.

"You fall off your bike, and you don't play three matches maybe, or maybe worse, maybe you break a leg ... There are a lot of things you have to give up to be a football player."

Mbappé suffered a hyperextension of his left knee during France's game with Türkiye on September 25, and was subsequently released by the national team.

ESPN has reported that his participation in Real Madrid's game with Villarreal this Saturday when LaLiga returns is in doubt, although he is expected to be fit to play Barcelona in El Clásico on Oct. 25.

- Kylian Mbappé, Ibrahima Konaté, Fede Valverde expected to be available for El Clásico - source

- Dembélé dismisses 'little squabbles' pitting him against Mbappé

- UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case

Mbappé has scored seven goals in seven league games for Madrid so far this season, but the team are already six points behind rivals Barça in the table.

He faced criticism in the Madrid media last season after being pictured on holiday on a yacht with his partner, while recovering from a hamstring injury.

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more
articles.description: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
articles.headlineJa: 2027年NFLドラフト第1ラウンドの指名順予想、トップ指名の確率など
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNのフットボール・パワー・インデックスが2027年NFLドラフト第1ラウンドの指名順を予想。各チームがトップ5、トップ10、そして1位で指名する確率も併せて公開している。
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

See more on the NFL draft

First-round picks that have been traded:

The Green Bay Packers' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade.

The Indianapolis Colts' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade.

The Los Angeles Rams' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade.

The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade.

articles.headline: Cowboys flip script after Rio loss with key win over Texans
articles.description: A week after everything went wrong late against the Ravens, Dallas rebounded with a winning drive Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: カウボーイズ、リオでの敗戦から巻き返し、テキサンズに重要勝利
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズ戦で終盤に不運が重なった1週間後、ダラスは日曜日の試合で勝ち越しドライブを決め、見事に復活した。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- One week after enduring a 10-hour flight home from Rio de Janeiro after a debilitating 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens, the 45-minute flight back home from Houston on Sunday night had to feel a lot better for the Dallas Cowboys.

Questions surrounded the Cowboys following the loss to the Ravens -- especially about coach Brian Schottenheimer, defensive coordinator Christian Parker, special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen, and how the coaches managed the final 28 seconds of a game they were 2 yards away from potentially winning.

Against the Houston Texans (0-4) on Sunday, the Cowboys were trailing 30-27 with 2:25 left, facing a 1-3 start to the season for the second straight year.

But quarterback Dak Prescott and receiver CeeDee Lamb helped lessen the temperature around the coaches and players by connecting on a 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds to go for a 34-30 must-have victory.

"Rio doesn't define us as a football team, as a coaching staff here," Schottenheimer said. "I think I was very upfront and honest with that, but I wanted this game. Why? Because these guys came back off a 10-hour trip. The Ravens, I think, played at home today. We played on the road. We play Thursday night [against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers].

"We'll play anybody anywhere and we're looking forward to that, but Rio had nothing to do with this game. This game stood by itself."

But the fate of a season might have been on the line with a loss. Since 2000, the Cowboys have never opened a season with one victory in the first month of the season and finished above .500. The best they have done is last year's 7-9-1 in Schottenheimer's first season.

In the first half, a Cowboys' offense that wants to be considered "The Greatest Offense There Is" failed to score a touchdown. In the second half, they scored touchdowns on their first three possessions, then Prescott delivered with the late winning drive.

In certain moments, the defense was better. Linebacker Rashan Gary had his first sack in 12 games, dating to last season with the Green Bay Packers. Defensive end Quinnen Williams had his first sack of the season, dropping C.J. Stroud for an 11-yard loss in the fourth quarter. In the first three games, the Cowboys had two sacks. They had three Sunday.

But the unit still gave up eight pass plays of at least 20 yards.

Schottenheimer wasn't concerned about his decision at the end of the half when he opted to have Brandon Aubrey attempt a 65-yard field goal despite the Texans being out of timeouts. When Aubrey's kick hooked a little left, the Texans were able to convert a field goal of their own to take a 16-6 halftime lead.

"We felt very comfortable that Brandon would make that kick," Schottenheimer said. "And at that point in the game, I had no question that if for some reason he missed it, that we had plenty of time to fight back."

articles.headline: How Steve Gleason's punt block unified New Orleans, Falcons-Saints rivalry
articles.description: Ahead of Monday's Falcons-Saints game, players and coaches reflect on the storm, the game and a play from 20 years ago.
articles.headlineJa: スティーブ・グリーソンのパントブロックがいかにニューオーリンズを団結させ、ファルコンズ対セインツのライバル関係を築いたか
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜日のファルコンズ対セインツ戦を前に、選手やコーチたちが、かつての嵐、あの試合、そして20年前のあの一プレーを振り返る。
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Saints and Atlanta Falcons will carry the weight of history between them when they meet at the Caesars' Superdome on Monday night (8:15 ET, ESPN).

Hurricane Katrina made landfall along the Gulf Coast on Aug. 29, 2005, killing more than 1,300 people, decimating the region and impacting lives in the area forever.

The Superdome, which was used as a shelter of last resort during the storm, was inoperable for more than a year because of extreme roof damage.

The indoor stadium reopened to the public on Sept. 25, 2006 ahead of a Week 3 game featuring the Saints and Falcons on "Monday Night Football." Former Saints quarterback Archie Manning and a group of first responders were among those who ceremonially ushered fans back into the Dome ahead of a performance by the Goo Goo Dolls. The pregame celebration continued inside with performances by Green Day and U2.

Pregame shots showed the building surrounded by water in the days after the storm before transitioning to a live shot showing fans counting down the seconds until reopening, clearly ready to move forward to a new chapter.

While the fanfare included former President George H.W. Bush, who oversaw the coin toss, the real star of the night was a 29-year-old Saints player named Steve Gleason. The core special-teamer blocked Michael Koenen's punt less than 90 seconds into the game.

Gleason came rushing up the middle, stretched up his arms and hit the football with a solid thwack! Gleason's teammate Curtis Deloatch ran down the ball and fell on it in the end zone for a touchdown.

The momentum never let up. When the game was over, ESPN analyst Stuart Scott noted "not a soul has left this building," as the camera panned a stadium still packed with fans.

That block -- in a game that snowballed into a 23-3 Saints rout -- would make history, eventually being ranked No. 28 on the NFL's "100 Greatest Plays" list. It symbolized a new beginning for New Orleans.

There have been 5,216 regular-season games, 45,983 punts and 247 punts blocked since that night. Perhaps none of those blocked punts have had as much of an impact on one city as the one by Gleason, whose moment is now commemorated in a statue outside the Superdome titled "Rebirth."

It was the start of a run of success for the Saints, who made it to the NFC Championship Game that season and went on to win Super Bowl XLIV during the 2009 season.

For the Falcons, it was another chapter in a rivalry that burns bright 20 years after that game.

Gleason, who was diagnosed with ALS in 2011, became a hero in New Orleans and still considers the blocked punt a defining moment of his life.

"Here's what the blocked punt means to me now. It means I'm alive," Gleason told NFL Network's Steve Wyche. "... If I don't block that punt I'd be dead. Before the punt block I was just a pretty good special teams player, but I wasn't Lou Gehrig or Stephen Hawking. I was just a dude. If I don't block that punt, I'm just another has-been football player

articles.headline: With Edgerrin Cooper out, Evan Williams shines for Packers
articles.description: The Packers lost one of their two young defensive stars in Cooper (Achilles), but Williams delivered a big game.
articles.headlineJa: エジャリン・クーパーの欠場、エヴァン・ウィリアムズがパッカーズで躍進
articles.descriptionJa: パッカーズは若きディフェンスのスター2人のうちの1人であるクーパー（アキレス腱）を欠いたが、ウィリアムズが素晴らしい活躍を見せた。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Evan Williams has had interceptions before. Four of them in his first 32 NFL regular-season games before Sunday to be exact. So while the Green Bay Packers safety would like the football he inadvertently discarded after interception No. 5 came early in Sunday's 17-14 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, it was the sack -- his first in the NFL -- on the final series that might have been more meaningful.

Three times on the final three defensive plays of the game, coordinator Jonathan Gannon called blitzes. Three times, he sent Williams. On the first, Williams came unblocked and sacked rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. The second forced a quick pass for a short completion. And on the third, Williams got home again and had Daniels in his grasp when the quarterback flung the ball away.

Game over.

Not only did the Packers (2-2) come away with a much-needed win, but they may also have found a way to make up for the loss of linebacker Edgerrin Cooper, who left the game in the second half with a likely season-ending Achilles injury.

Yes, the Packers have leaders such as linebacker Zaire Franklin and safety Xavier McKinney. And eventually they will get star edge rusher Micah Parsons back. But Cooper and Williams were the young stars on this defense, both members of the 2024 draft class, and now one of them is likely out of the picture.

Gannon might not rush Williams as much from the safety spot as he did with Cooper as a linebacker, but for Gannon to give Williams that responsibility -- and for Williams to deliver -- could be a sign of what's to come without Cooper.

"Shoutout to that guy just because he always preaches players not plays in the biggest situations," Williams said of Gannon. "For him to call my number in that type of situation, it means a lot to me. To understand the coach has that type of trust in you in the big situations, when you have to make a play, that you're the number he calls, that means everything. Moving forward, yeah, it means everything."

It capped the kind of performance by Williams that the Packers are going to need. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper took over for Cooper at linebacker Sunday, but Williams took over as playmaker. He already had that first-quarter interception, which wasn't granted until replay overturned the call of incomplete on the field, but Williams finished with seven tackles, the sack (which was one of two QB hits) and two pass breakups.

"Hell of a game," McKinney said.

Williams' two pressures on the final drive gave him six for the season after recording two in his first two seasons. Part of that is opportunity. But with opportunity comes responsibility.

"He can be really f---ing good," McKinney said. "I think just the progression that I've seen him make from when he first came here to where he's at now, he's a mature player. articles.headline: Joe Burrow after 2nd straight loss: Not 'Armageddon'
articles.description: Another Burrow fourth-quarter turnover helped bring the Bengals back to .500, but optimism remains.
articles.headlineJa: ジョー・バロウ、2連敗を受けても「アルマゲドン（世界の終わり）ではない」
articles.descriptionJa: 第4クォーターでのバロウの再びのターンオーバーにより、ベンガルズは勝率5割まで後退したが、依然として楽観視している。
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- Even if the exact message was muffled, the intensity from Cincinnati Bengals coach Zac Taylor certainly wasn't.

In the immediate aftermath of the team's second straight loss, a 22-17 home defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Taylor's voice could be heard bellowing through the wall that separates the locker room and the media room where news conferences are conducted. Beyond the volume, Taylor's remarks were among the longest following a home loss in recent memory.

When the eighth-year coach left the locker room to speak to the reporters, Taylor characterized it as encouragement to a team that will need to fight through one of the season's most important stretches.

For the second straight year, the Bengals are back to .500 after Week 4 following two wins to open the season. But the stakes are a bit higher this year.

Breaking a three-year playoff drought, if not at least winning a game or two in mid-January, will be needed to eliminate the mounting pressure on Taylor and the franchise. After Sunday's loss, the Bengals are now tasked with rebuilding momentum and making this season feel promising again.

"We had our opportunities in the last two weeks, but this isn't Armageddon or anything," quarterback Joe Burrow said after the game. "We're still in a great spot (and) feel really good about our team."

If anything, the comments show Taylor's postgame message resonated throughout the locker room following a comeback attempt that fell 12 yards short. The Bengals trailed 22-10 with 6:35 left in the fourth quarter before Burrow and the Bengals made a late push at an improbable victory.

After a touchdown and a defensive stop, the Bengals made it all the way into Jacksonville's red zone before running back Chase Brown was stopped on the 12-yard line on a fourth-down catch, one yard shy of a new set of downs to keep the drive alive.

And instead of a win that could have positioned the Bengals well, Cincinnati was left talking about familiar woes.

According to Next Gen Stats, Cincinnati missed 12 tackles on defense. Jacksonville had six. The Jaguars also had 143 yards after the catch. Both issues plagued the Bengals in 2025.

"They hit some checkdowns; and checkdowns, they're not supposed to convert a (third down)," linebacker Barrett Carter said.

Offensively, the lack of a run game was an issue against Jacksonville. The Bengals had 15 carries for 23 yards. Burrow had 58 dropbacks, tied for the fourth-most in his career, according to ESPN Research. And in the quarterback's mind, that number could have been higher.

His response to the idea of having more balanced play calls?

"Let's throw it more," Burrow said.

There is one other trend that is now becoming more noticeable. Since the start of the 2024 season, Burrow now leads the NFL in most turnovers in the fourth quarter or overtime, according to ESPN Research.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Bayern brace for tough contract talks with Olise
articles.description: Bayern Munich could be facing an uphill battle to sign winger Michael Olise to a new contract. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：バイエルン、オリセとの厳しい契約交渉に備える
articles.descriptionJa: バイエルン・ミュンヘンは、ウィングのマイケル・オリセと新契約を結ぶために苦戦を強いられる可能性がある。Transfer Talkが最新情報をお届けする。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich are bracing for tough contract talks with star winger Michael Olise, while Chelsea lead the race for AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich are concerned about talks to renew Michael Olise's contract, as the winger hasn't yet told them if he even wants to stay in Bavaria, as reported by Sport Bild. The Bundesliga club is preparing for a very difficult negotiation with the representatives of the 24-year-old. One of the sticking points is that the France international wants a release clause in his new contract, something both Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala have. Bayern are willing to offer a mega contract that will run until 2032 but want an answer by next summer.

- Chelsea are leading the race to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who is also attracting strong interest from Liverpool and Arsenal, as reported by The Telegraph. Elsewhere, TEAMtalk have suggested that Real Madrid are considering becoming involved in the race for the 23-year-old after watching him closely in recent weeks. Los Blancos have watched Scott at least three times, including his first England start in the Three Lions' 7-0 victory over Croatia.

- Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport has offered an insight into the names Roma are looking at as they aim to sign a winger. In the summer, they looked at Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling and Chelsea's Jamie Gittens, who have both had a lack of game time since the summer transfer window shut so could be available for less than was demanded before. They also want Real Madrid's Endrick, hoping for a Donyell Malen-style deal where they have a loan with the option to make it permanent, and they aren't alarmed by AC Milan's interest. Frosinone's Giorgi Kvernadze is another player of interest.

- Juventus see Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Højbjerg as the leader Luciano Spalletti needs, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. They have previously looked at Leon Goretzka and Franck Kessié, who ended up at Aston Villa and Atalanta respectively, but remain keen on signing an older head for their midfield so are turning to the man who is captain for both Marseille and Denmark. There have already been exploratory contacts made about the 31-year-old, while Teun Koopmeiners is the main candidate to leave so he can come in.

- Juventus have recently made a move for Frosinone goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani and Inter Milan are monitoring him, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. Inter chief executive Beppe Marotta has insisted on a mix of foreign and Italian players, emphasizing the importance of a strong Italy squad. I Nerazzurri could decide to loan out the 22-year-old if they sign him, and they are also looking at Alessandro Romano, who is on loan at Cagliari from Roma.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグのどの選手が代表ウィーク中に負傷したか？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズン最初の代表ウィークにおける、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースとアップデート。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Pistons' Jalen Duren happy to return despite prolonged talks
articles.description: Despite a prolonged negotiation that appeared to turn sour at times, Jalen Duren said he is relieved and excited to return to Detroit.
articles.headlineJa: ピストンズのジェイレン・デュレン、長期にわたる交渉を経て復帰を喜ぶ
articles.descriptionJa: 時には険悪なムードに陥った長期の交渉を経て、ジェイレン・デュレンはデトロイトに復帰できることに安堵と喜びを感じていると語った。
articles.body:
Jalen Duren was both relieved and excited after signing a new five-year, $200 million deal to return to the Detroit Pistons after a contract negotiation that he said took "longer than both he and the organization anticipated."

But during his first news conference after signing his new deal, he wanted to clarify narratives that emerged during the negotiation that he said did not represent how he felt about the team, repeating that he was happy in Detroit and excited to return to the team.

"Detroit has become a home for me, this is where I live full-time," Duren told reporters at the team's practice facility on Sunday afternoon. "The city has embraced me as well as I've embraced the city.

"This process took way longer than any of us really wanted. Longer than I wanted, and I'm sure longer than the organization wanted. But [the Pistons] have a job to do as well as my team and my agency have a job to do to make the best outcome for both sides. I feel like we've done that."

 

Duren missed media day and the first few practices of training camp this week after a four-month long standoff between he and the Pistons over the value of his new contract. They eventually came to an agreement on a fully guaranteed contract late Thursday night, ahead of the deadline for him to accept a one-year qualifying offer.

On Sunday, sitting next to team president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon, Duren said he wanted to be in Detroit for the rest of his career.

"There's a business component that it took me time to realize and understand because this is my first time going through it," the 22-year old All-NBA center said. "I can admit that I have flaws. We all do and we're here to work on it.

"I don't think this should be a negative outlook or looked at as something bad has happened. I think we look at it as something great has happened. I'm locked in with a team and a core who has potential that's going through the roof and I'm super excited for what's to come."

The standoff over Duren's contract came following the best regular season of the young center's career. He averaged a career high in points (19.5), made his first All-Star team and was named to the All-NBA third team as the Pistons became the top seed in the Eastern Conference. But he struggled mightily in the postseason, dropping to 10.2 points per game in 14 playoff games before Detroit's second-round exit.

Duren said he took a step back to get his head right following a postseason he described as "humbling," and he acknowledged his own silence allowed narratives to emerge in his absence. But he said he stayed focused in the offseason on getting better and acknowledging his flaws.

"Last season was some of my highest moments in my career and some of my lowest," Duren said. "I'm willing to acknowledge that. articles.headline: Spurs' Tobias Harris to miss preseason with left calf strain
articles.description: Spurs free agent acquisition Tobias Harris sustained a calf strain during camp that has him questionable for the team's Oct. 20 season opener vs. OKC.
articles.headlineJa: スパーズのトバイアス・ハリス、左ふくらはぎの挫傷でプレシーズンを欠場
articles.descriptionJa: スパーズがフリーエージェントで獲得したトバイアス・ハリスが、キャンプ中にふくらはぎを挫傷。10月20日のOKC戦でのシーズン開幕戦への出場は不透明となっている。
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- The San Antonio Spurs announced before tipoff of their intrasquad scrimmage Sunday that free-agent acquisition Tobias Harris suffered a strained left calf during training camp that leaves him questionable for the Oct. 20 season opener against Oklahoma City.

A teams spokesman said that Harris would miss Sunday's scrimmage and will be re-evaluated after the preseason.

Harris, 34, signed a two-year, $31 million deal in July to join the Spurs, leaving a Detroit Pistons team that he helped lead a franchise turnaround over the previous two seasons.

A productive veteran lauded for knocking down shots and floor spacing in the frontcourt, Harris was expected to begin the season in San Antonio's starting lineup.

Harris averaged 13.5 points and 5.6 rebounds per game in his second stint in Detroit, as the Pistons improved from one of the league's worst teams two years ago to capturing 60 victories last season and advancing in the playoffs for the first time since 2008.

Harris served as one of the few veterans on a Pistons team that ranked as one of the NBA's youngest. The veteran signed a two-year $52 million deal with Detroit in 2024 as a free agency, after spending six seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Liverpool haven't opened the door to the 19-year-old leaving, but Juventus aren't giving up on him.

More clubs are showing an interest in Nijstad and have started travelling to scout him.

articles.headline: Who most deserves the Ballon d'Or? Whittling down the 30-man short list
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane are the three favorites to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but who actually deserves to win it?
articles.headlineJa: バロンドールに最もふさわしいのは誰か？30人の候補リストを絞り込む
articles.descriptionJa: キリアン・エムバペ、ラミン・ヤマル、ハリー・ケインが2026年バロンドールの3大本命だが、真に受賞に値するのは誰か？
articles.body:
For most of the past 15 years, there was really no point in campaigning for the men's Ballon d'Or -- it was going to the more obnoxiously successful of two men, Lionel Messi (eight-time winner) or Cristiano Ronaldo (five). Their personal -- and sometimes club -- rivalry defined the sport, to the point where even a rising star like Kylian Mbappé openly admitted he wasn't as good as them.

"It's not only me who knows that," he told writer Simon Kuper in "The Barcelona Complex." "Everyone knows it. If you tell yourself that you'll do better than them, it's beyond ego or determination -- it's lack of awareness. Those players are incomparable. They have broken all laws of statistics."

"I can't top them" probably isn't the healthiest thing in the world for a megastar to tell himself, but with Messi and Ronaldo finally having aged out of the competition -- Ronaldo hasn't finished in the top three of the voting in the 2020s, and Messi's final win came in 2023 -- now's the time to pounce.

Mbappé wants it. Lamine Yamal has said he wants it. Harry Kane thinks winning it would be "amazing." They're the three betting favorites for the award -- Kane's and Yamal's odds are both at +100 after a recent rise from Yamal, while Mbappé is at a longer +1000 -- but who actually deserves it?

After some late PR campaigns from players and clubs, voting for the award closed on Monday. It will go to the player who achieved the most between the beginning of the 2025-26 club season and the end of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Thirty players were officially nominated, but based on who has won the award in the past, we can narrow the field pretty quickly.

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

- Lindop: Liverpool can't afford to be without Isak, Gakpo in October

Eliminate anyone who played for Real Madrid last season

Eliminated: Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior

I'm sorry, but we have to start here. The three players above are all dynamite, and two have come pretty close to winning the award already -- Mbappé was 192 points behind Messi in 2023, and Vinícius was only 41 points behind Rodri in 2024.

Mbappé is indeed No. 3 in the betting odds, and his scorpionlike quick strike capabilities might make him the most terrifying player in the world. At any point, it feels as if you could be about eight seconds from a Mbappé goal. He's great.

He has also been part of a terribly disappointing club team for two straight years. Since Mbappé joined Real Madrid, the only trophies they've won were the UEFA Super Cup and the FIFA Intercontinental Cup in 2024, trophies tied to accomplishments of the team before his arrival.

Real Madrid have finished behind Barcelona in both of Mbappé's seasons, and after winning the UEFA Champions League in the season before his arrival, they haven't made it past the quarterfinals with him. The Ballon d'Or isn't for club underachiever

articles.headline: Lakers' Ziaire Williams proposes to longtime girlfriend at Bruno Mars tour
articles.description: The singer complemented the proposal during his second of five Inglewood shows.
articles.headlineJa: レイカーズのザイア・ウィリアムズ、ブルーノ・マーズのツアーで長年の恋人にプロポーズ
articles.descriptionJa: イングルウッドでの5公演のうち2公演目、歌手のブルーノ・マーズがこのプロポーズを盛り上げた。
articles.body:
Pop superstar Bruno Mars knows how to put on a good show. But on Friday night, one audience member seemed to steal the show from the 16-time Grammy winner.

As Mars performed "Marry You" during his second night of five in Inglewood, California, for "The Romantic Tour," Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams found the perfect moment to make a promise for forever.

On the floor level of SoFi Stadium, Williams got down on bended knee as Mars sang the words "I think I wanna marry you," lining up his question -- "Will you marry me?" -- with the lyrics.

As Williams proposed to his teary-eyed girlfriend, model Paris Timan, Mars blended his singing with his excitement, crooning, "Please say I do I do I do."

After Timan -- who seemed to be in shock -- said yes, Mars continued singing through the song's conclusion while the couple shared a hug as the audience erupted in cheers.

Timan will be part of two new beginnings for Williams. In July, the 25-year-old signed a one-year, $3 million deal with the Lakers after a 2025-26 season in which he posted 10.2 points and 2.4 rebounds per game in 54 games with the Brooklyn Nets.

And the next part? Planning the rest of their lives together. Nothing screams "fairy tale" more than a proposal to a Mars love song.

articles.headline: LeBron James calls scrimmage 'great first step' for new-look 76ers
articles.description: Throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep to watch LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and the rest of the 76ers take part in Saturday's scrimmage.
articles.headlineJa: レブロン・ジェームズ、新体制の76ersにとって練習試合は「素晴らしい第一歩」と評価
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日の練習試合に出場したレブロン・ジェームズ、ジェイレン・ブラウン、そして76ersのメンバーを見るため、多くのファンが10列以上の長い列を作って待機した。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- It might have been the basketball equivalent of a dress rehearsal, but the 76ers' intrasquad scrimmage Saturday certainly gave a promising glimpse of what could be in store when the curtain actually comes up for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Philadelphia hosted its annual Blue-White game in front of approximately 10,000 fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena, moving the exhibition from their G League affiliate's home in Delaware to accommodate the added interest in the new-look team.

While throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep in the atrium an hour before the noon start, there was plenty of on-court action from LeBron James, Jaylen Brown & Co. to enjoy as soon as the scrimmage started.

"To be able to take what we've done on the practice floor, bring it to a game floor situation around our fans ... it was a great first step in the direction we're trying to go," James said.

Longtime Sixers public address announcer Matt Cord, who had retired before deciding to come back once Philadelphia had its historic summer, announced the starters for the Blue team.

First Tyrese Maxey, then VJ Edgecombe, then Brown, then James and then the man in the middle who has been with the franchise for 13 years.

"7-2 from Cameroon, No. 21, Joel 'The Processsss' Embiiddddd!" Cord bellowed.

"It doesn't matter who gets announced first, last, second, third," Embiid said.

But the cheers that followed every name did mean something to him.

"We love the fans," Embiid said. "We want them, and we need them to be part of this. I mentioned it at media day: It's already hard enough to win as a group that gets together for the first year. So we're going to need all we can, whether it's from everybody in this building, the fans, the outside people, we're going to need to get together. We're going to need all the support possible."

The Sixers didn't keep an official box score, but the stats mattered far less than some of the sequences that showed the early chemistry that is developing after a week of training camp, including James finding a trailing Embiid for an above-the-break 3.

"Guys are going to use their speed against people and try to score a quick basket, and if we don't have anything, I'm the trail guy," Embiid said matter-of-factly.

Both Maxey and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope delivered feeds to James for alley-oop dunks that the 41-year-old star finished with ease. Embiid got his 7-foot frame to lift high enough to both block springy second-year guard Edgecombe and have a dunk of his own.

"Pretty good, not bad," a noticeably slimmed-down Embiid said when asked how he felt physically compared to last season. Then he showed his sense of humor is as strong as ever.

"That's probably the last dunk of my career," Embiid said with a smirk.

While James has had only four official Sixers practices, plus the scrimmage, it was enough for him to conclude that Embiid is a different player than the guy he won a gold medal with at the Paris Olympics two summers ago.

articles.headline: Cucurella: Too soon to judge Mourinho's Madrid amid poor start
articles.description: Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.
articles.headlineJa: ククレリャ：不調なスタートを切った今、モウリーニョ率いるマドリードを判断するには時期尚早
articles.descriptionJa: マルク・ククレリャは、新監督ジョゼ・モウリーニョのもと、レアル・マドリードが望んでいたようなシーズン開幕を迎えられていないことを認めているが、チームの評価は今ではなくシーズン終了時にすべきだと述べている。
articles.body:
Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.

Madrid have suffered two defeats in their opening seven LaLiga games, against Real Betis and Atlético Madrid, leaving them six points behind early leaders Barcelona.

- Torres forced out of Spain squad; Madrid's Espí gets 1st call-up

- De la Fuente says beloved Yamal puts 'magic' at service of Spain

- UEFA receives Madrid dossier on Barça-Negreira case

Cucurella, speaking in a news conference on Friday while on international duty with world champions Spain, said Madrid's new project needs time to take shape.

"It's all a process," Cucurella said. "With the national team, the foundations have been laid over many years -- with the [same] coach, too.

"At Madrid, we have just started with a new manager and it's too soon to speak. Some players only had a week-long preseason before starting.

"The beginning of the season hasn't been what we all hoped for, but it's a process and we will see where we are at the end of the campaign."

Cucurella has picked up where he left off for Spain at the World Cup in the summer, impressing in UEFA Nations League victories over England and Croatia during the last week.

It has led to suggestions the left back -- a €55 million ($62m) summer signing for Madrid from Chelsea -- is better suited to playing for his country than his club.

"It's not even been 10 games yet," Cucurella responded. "There are things to improve [with Madrid], of course. We basically had no preseason, while it's a new club for me.

"I have to adapt to my new teammates and give my best so that the player you see with the national team is the same player with Real Madrid."

Cucurella's form for Chelsea and Spain not only prompted Madrid to sign him in the summer, but also led to him being named among the 30 nominees to win this year's Ballon d'Or.

He is also in the rare position of playing alongside two of the favourites -- Kylian Mbappé with Madrid and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal with Spain -- but would not pick between the two.

"If it was up to me to vote, I would vote for myself," he joked when asked to name his winner.

"But no, two of the candidates to win it are teammates, so who whoever wins it, I will be happy."

Cucurella and Spain are back in action on Saturday when they host Czechia in Oviedo looking to make it three wins from three in the Nations League.

They then close the extended international break with a trip to Croatia on Tuesday.
